figures.finding: Under Schedule 6 of the Income Tax Act 1992 as read, a resident individual's taxable income is taxed at 30%, less a rebate of $15 for each completed week (up to 52), so that income up to a set level bears no tax; later amendments (2008, 2017, 2019) were not read.

rebate.nonResident: increased by one third, weeks present only

value.version: Act 5 of 1992 text as hosted by ICNL

figures.applies: Resident individuals (text of uncertain revision date)

sources.said: 1. In relation to any person in any year, income tax shall be payable at the rates set out below in respect of that person's taxable income for that year: % of taxable income (a) Taxable income of a resident individual in their personal capacity 30%

year (not exceeding 52 in aggregate) for which the person was a taxpayer a rebate of: $15 Provided that: … b) the purpose of the rebate is that for any person who is a resident individual, who is entitled to the rebate in relation to any year, a zero rate of income tax applies to so much of that person's taxable income as does not exceed the specified level of taxable income (as defined in section 2); and (c) where the individual is non resident, the rebate: (i) shall be increased by one third; and (ii) shall only be available in relation to completed weeks of presence in Tuvalu.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year, and the annual return of income is due within 2 months of its end (by 28 or 29 February) unless the Secretary extends the time.
figures.applies: Income Tax Act Cap. 26.16, 2008 Revised Edition, ss. 2 and 41(6).

sources.said: “year” means the calendar year: … Where the person had not been accorded an extension of time pursuant … to section 43, within 2 months of the end of the year

figures.finding: A service fee paid to a non-resident for work done in Tuvalu is non-resident withholding income: the payer withholds 15% of the gross fee (less under a treaty), and the non-resident owes the greater of that withholding and the tax on the fee figured as ordinary taxable income; for services rendered outside Tuvalu the 15% is final.

value.final: final for services outside Tuvalu; otherwise the greater of 15% and the ordinary tax

figures.finding: Consumption Tax falls on taxable supplies, services included, by a person registered or liable to register, which a person must do when taxable supplies reach $100,000 in a 12-month period; the rate is set by Regulation within 3% to 10%.

figures.finding: Every employee in Tuvalu is a member of the Tuvalu National Provident Fund: the employee pays 13% of gross monthly earnings and the employer 10% (the TNPF's employers' page reads 'a minimum of 13%'), due by the 15th of the next month; an employer may add up to 3% more; the self-employed may join voluntarily.
